open_points.subject: owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: Which cookie attributes, host/path scope and trusted scheme determination enforce these guarantees, especially when local access uses HTTP and remote HTTPS may terminate at a proxy?
options: Always use Secure, HttpOnly and a host-only cookie with a fixed Registry path
Use Secure conditionally based on a trusted deployment setting or forwarded scheme
Treat “own origin” as the whole host despite cookies not being scoped by port
open_points.default_guess: Use a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie and require Registry to receive HTTPS directly.

open_points.subject: owner-session sign-out concurrency
open_points.text: “A sign-out is applied in turn with the session's other requests that change it: one admitted before it completes its change to the store, and leaves nothing in the ended session.”
open_points.question: If a request passes the arrival-time session check before sign-out but acquires the session lock after sign-out, must that request still change the store, or must it be refused because the session record is then gone?
options: Every request admitted before sign-out completes, even if it takes the lock later
The session-lock order decides, so a request ordered after sign-out is refused
Sign-out waits for all previously admitted requests before taking effect
open_points.default_guess: The session-lock order decides and a request ordered after sign-out is refused.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never as the values themselves”
open_points.question: What canonical encoding, field presence rules and digest algorithm define equality of confirmation-bound inputs across rendering and submission?
options: A specified canonical binary or JSON encoding plus a specified cryptographic digest
The implementation's ordinary serialization and digest
Store a random confirmation value plus the original inputs instead of an input digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a specified canonical encoding with explicit absent-value markers and SHA-256.

open_points.subject: import upload side effects
open_points.text: “Registry reads it as data and answers, without changing anything” versus “The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it”
open_points.question: Does a successful upload count as a state change to the OwnerSession, with serialization, CSRF and last-request effects, while changing only no durable domain records?
options: It changes temporary OwnerSession state but no durable store state
It changes nothing and the client must upload the file again at confirmation
The uploaded file is durable despite the later memory-only rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a serialized change to temporary OwnerSession state and interpret “without changing anything” as no durable domain-store change.

open_points.subject: import mapping contents
open_points.text: “the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display name and alias each will arrive under” and “The owner sees exactly what will arrive before anything does”
open_points.question: Must the mapping also show the imported object and all other facts that will arrive, including source instants, status, pointer references and statuses, or are those accepted without being displayed?
options: Show every imported fact and every generated or reset fact
Show only the explicitly listed summary while importing the remaining facts unseen
Show object and personal facts but summarize technical history
open_points.default_guess: Show every imported fact or its explicit deterministic transformation before confirmation.

open_points.subject: replacement after malformed upload
open_points.text: “a refused upload — too large or unreadable — replaces nothing” and “A file that ... holds two project records with one id ... is refused whole at upload”
open_points.question: When a readable upload is refused for an upload-time structural defect rather than size or unreadability, does it preserve or replace the previously uploaded file in that session?
options: Every refused upload preserves the previous file
Only too-large or unreadable uploads preserve it; other refused uploads clear or replace it
Every attempted upload first clears the previous file
open_points.default_guess: Every refused upload preserves the previous accepted file.

open_points.subject: import file identity
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)”
open_points.question: Which exact bytes are digested, with which algorithm, and is identity based on the uploaded byte stream or a canonicalized parsed representation?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a specified cryptographic algorithm
Digest a canonical serialization of parsed import data
Leave the algorithm and representation release-specific
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with SHA-256.

open_points.subject: lost accepted-import response
open_points.text: “The import answers once its transaction commits, listing for each Customer it made its v1 value and the customer_ref minted for it” and “While the closure exists ... confirming an import [is] refused”
open_points.question: How can the owner recover the v1-value-to-customer_ref mapping if the transaction commits but its answer is lost, given that a retry is refused and a non-tax-id v1 value is kept nowhere?
options: A retry of the same confirmed file returns the committed result
The closure durably stores the result mapping for later reading
The result is intentionally unrecoverable through Registry
open_points.default_guess: Store the result mapping with the closure and return it for an exact replay or owner read.

open_points.subject: import object conversion
open_points.text: “An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers” while State 1 says “the import carries [the object] inside its project”
open_points.question: How are the v1 project's address and other source fields converted into the required embedded Object, including absent kind and characteristics, and which conversion failures refuse the import?
options: A fixed field-by-field conversion declared with the import format
The owner supplies every Object value in the mapping
Copy only the address and leave optional Object facts absent
open_points.default_guess: Copy the v1 address into the required Object address and leave unsupported optional facts absent, under an explicit mapping rule.

open_points.subject: configuration variable names
open_points.text: “the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_” and “It holds exactly these items and no other”
open_points.question: What exact environment-variable name corresponds to each required item, including the four service tokens?
options: State 2 declares all exact names
States 5 or 6 must declare the names before implementation
Each implementation chooses names under the prefix
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed names for the store, backup directory, backup key, owner credential and each named service token.

open_points.subject: configuration well-formedness
open_points.text: “each well formed”
open_points.question: What makes each location, owner credential, service token and backup key well formed beyond the separately stated presence and minimum length checks?
options: Only paths parse and secrets meet their byte-length rule
A declared character encoding and syntax applies to every item
Each secret is arbitrary bytes supplied through an encoding such as base64
open_points.default_guess: Treat paths as valid absolute filesystem paths and secrets as base64-encoded arbitrary bytes.

open_points.subject: secret length measurement
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long”
open_points.question: How are bytes obtained from environment-variable text for length, equality and authentication: UTF-8 bytes, decoded base64/hex bytes, or another representation?
options: Measure UTF-8 encoded environment text
Decode a required base64 representation and measure the decoded secret
Measure characters despite the word bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require base64 and measure the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: backup encryption and authentication
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “it records, readable without its key”
open_points.question: What encryption format, algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation and authentication protect the encrypted body and the readable metadata?
options: A versioned authenticated-encryption container with authenticated cleartext metadata
Implementation-selected encryption with no cross-release format guarantee
Encryption without metadata authentication
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD container with a fresh random nonce and authenticate the cleartext metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: backup retention after a failed run
open_points.text: “Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before” versus “a failed or missed run lengthens both [erasure propagation and recovery loss]”
open_points.question: Does a run whose backup creation or verification fails but whose deletion step succeeds still remove expired backups and therefore preserve the erasure-propagation bound?
options: Yes; backup failure lengthens recovery loss but not erasure propagation when cleanup succeeds
No; any failed run retains old backups and lengthens both
Only specified classes of failure permit cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Run cleanup after creation or verification failure; only a cleanup failure or missed run lengthens erasure propagation.

open_points.subject: backup deletion failures
open_points.text: “it deletes every kept backup ... and every file ... that cannot be read as a backup” and “A step that fails ... writes a diagnostic”
open_points.question: If deletion of one eligible file fails, does Registry continue deleting the others, in what order, and does the run have one diagnostic or one per failed file?
options: Best-effort deletion of every eligible file, reporting every failure
Stop at the first deletion failure
Retry failed deletions within the same run
open_points.default_guess: Attempt every eligible deletion in deterministic name order and report each failure without stopping the remaining cleanup.

open_points.subject: one-day recovery bound
open_points.text: “a restore loses at most a day of changes”
open_points.question: What maximum backup-run duration or completion deadline makes the one-day bound true, since consecutive successful runs start 24 hours apart but may finish arbitrarily late?
options: Define the bound from backup start and require an atomic snapshot at 03:00
Set a maximum completion duration included in the recovery bound
Replace the bound with time since the last successfully completed backup
open_points.default_guess: Define the snapshot instant at the 03:00 run start and state recovery loss relative to the newest successful snapshot.

open_points.subject: backup prefixes across releases
open_points.text: “Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares”
open_points.question: May a later release change these prefixes, and if so how does it discover, display and delete backups made under earlier releases rather than orphaning them?
options: Prefixes are stable for all releases
Every release recognizes all earlier prefix versions
A release migration renames old backups before Registry starts
open_points.default_guess: Use stable version-independent prefixes and put format version inside the backup container.

open_points.subject: empty audit log backup metadata
open_points.text: “the last audit sequence number it holds” and “checks that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: What sequence value is recorded and what check passes for a new store whose audit log has no entries?
options: Record zero as the empty-log sentinel
Record no sequence value and require an empty log
Do not permit a backup until an audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record zero and require both an empty log and a last-ever sequence counter of zero.

open_points.subject: concurrent revision-moving actions
open_points.text: “A stated revision that is not the record's current one is refused as stale” and “Every action is atomic”
open_points.question: Are the revision check and update serialized or performed by an atomic compare-and-swap so that two concurrent changes stating the same current revision cannot both be accepted?
options: Exactly one commits and the other is stale
Both may commit in an implementation-defined order
Both may be accepted if their changed fields do not overlap
open_points.default_guess: Use an atomic revision compare-and-swap so exactly one change commits and every other concurrent change from that revision is stale.

open_points.subject: R0-89 backup guarantee
open_points.text: R0-89 says “Registry makes daily encrypted backups and checks each one,” while A18 says a stopped instance, an owner-only start, and an overlapping run make no backup for that 03:00
open_points.question: Is R0-89's daily-backup statement unconditional, or is it shorthand subject to every skip and failure condition in A18?
options: It is conditional shorthand governed by A18
A backup must be made every calendar day, with catch-up after a skip
Only stopped instances may miss a day; owner-only and overlap must catch up
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-89 as shorthand and make A18's explicit skip and failure rules controlling.
